{{Short description|Curve formed by connecting intermittent points on a rose curve}}
[[Image:Maurer Rose (n=7,d=29).svg|thumb|300px|A Maurer rose with ''n''&nbsp;=&nbsp;7 and ''d''&nbsp;=&nbsp;29]]
In geometry, '''Maurer rose''' is a curve consisting of some lines that connect some points on a [[rose curve]]. It was introduced by Peter M. Maurer in his article titled ''A Rose is a Rose...''.<ref name="mau">{{cite journal
 | last = Maurer | first = Peter M.
 | title = A Rose is a Rose...
 | journal = The American Mathematical Monthly
 | volume = 94 | issue = 7 | date = August–September 1987
 | pages = 631-645
 | doi = 10.2307/2322215
 | jstor = 2322215
 }}</ref>

==Definition==
Let ''r''&nbsp;=&nbsp;sin(''nθ'') be a [[rose curve|rose]] in the [[polar coordinate system]], where ''n'' is a positive integer. The rose has ''n'' petals if ''n'' is odd, and 2''n'' petals if ''n'' is even.

We then take 361 points on the rose:

: (sin(''nk''),&nbsp;''k'') (''k'' = 0, ''d'', 2''d'', 3''d'', ..., 360''d''),

where ''d'' is a positive integer and the angles are in [[Degree (angle)|degrees]], not [[radian]]s.

==Explanation==
A Maurer rose of the rose ''r''&nbsp;=&nbsp;sin(''nθ'') consists of the 360 lines successively connecting the above 361 points. Thus a Maurer rose is a [[Polygonal chain|polygonal curve]] with [[Vertex (geometry)|vertices]] on a rose.

A Maurer rose can be described as a closed route in the [[polar plane]]. A walker starts a journey from the origin, (0,&nbsp;0), and walks along a line to the point (sin(''nd''),&nbsp;''d''). Then, in the second leg of the journey, the walker walks along a line to the next point, (sin(''n''·2''d''),&nbsp;2''d''), and so on. Finally, in the final leg of the journey, the walker walks along a line, from (sin(''n''·359''d''),&nbsp;359''d'') to the ending point, (sin(''n''·360''d''),&nbsp;360''d''). The whole route is the Maurer rose of the rose ''r''&nbsp;=&nbsp;sin(''nθ''). A Maurer rose is a [[closed curve]] since the starting point, (0,&nbsp;0) and the ending point, (sin(''n''·360''d''),&nbsp;360''d''), coincide.

The following figure shows the evolution of a Maurer rose (''n''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2,&nbsp;''d''&nbsp;=&nbsp;29°).

[[Image:Evolution of a Maurer Rose.svg|750px]]

==Example implementation==

Using [[Python (programming language)|Python]]:
<syntaxhighlight lang="python">
import math, turtle

screen = turtle.Screen()
screen.setup(width=800, height=800, startx=0, starty=0)
screen.bgcolor("black")
pen = turtle.Turtle()
pen.speed(20)
n = 5
d = 97

pen.color("blue")
pen.pensize(0.5)
for theta in range(361):
    k = theta * d * math.pi / 180
    r = 300 * math.sin(n * k)
    x = r * math.cos(k)
    y = r * math.sin(k)
    pen.goto(x, y)

pen.color("red")
pen.pensize(4)
for theta in range(361):
    k = theta * math.pi / 180
    r = 300 * math.sin(n * k)
    x = r * math.cos(k)
    y = r * math.sin(k)
    pen.goto(x, y)
</syntaxhighlight>
